200 ) 201 } 202 ``` 203 204 ### Reading `searchParams` and `params` in Client Components 205 206 To use `searchParams` and `params` in a Client Component (which cannot be `async`), you can use React's [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) function to read the promise: 207 208 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 209 'use client' 210 211 import { use } from 'react' 212 213 export default function Page({ 214 params, 215 searchParams, 216 }: { 217 params: Promise<{ slug: string }> 218 searchParams: Promise<{ [key: string]: string | string[] | undefined }> 219 }) { 220 const { slug } = use(params) 221 const { query } = use(searchParams) 222 } 223 ``` 224 225 ```js filename="app/page.js" switcher 226 'use client' 227 228 import { use } from 'react' 229 230 export default function Page({ params, searchParams }) { 231 const { slug } = use(params) 232 const { query } = use(searchParams) 233 } 234 ``` 235 236 ## Version History 237 238 | Version | Changes | 239 | ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | 240 | `v15.0.0-RC` | `params` and `searchParams` are now promises. A [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#150) is available. | 241 | `v13.0.0` | `page` introduced. | 242

1 --- 2 title: layout.js 3 description: API reference for the layout.js file. 4 --- 5 6 The `layout` file is used to define a layout in your Next.js application. 7 8 ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.tsx" switcher 9 export default function DashboardLayout({ 10 children, 11 }: { 12 children: React.ReactNode 13 }) { 14 return
{children}
15 } 16 ``` 17 18 ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.js" switcher 19 export default function DashboardLayout({ children }) { 20 return
{children}
21 } 22 ``` 23 24 In the [component hierarchy](/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure#component-hierarchy), `layout.js` is the outermost component in a route segment. It wraps `template.js`, `error.js`, `loading.js`, `not-found.js`, and `page.js`. 25 26 A **root layout** is the top-most layout in the root `app` directory. It is used to define the `` and `` tags and other globally shared UI. 27 28 ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher 29 export default function RootLayout({ 30 children, 31 }: { 32 children: React.ReactNode 33 }) { 34 return ( 35 36 {children} 37 38 ) 39 } 40 ``` 41 42 ```jsx filename="app/layout.js" switcher 43 export default function RootLayout({ children }) { 44 return ( 45 46 {children} 47 48 ) 49 } 50 ``` 51 52 ## Reference 53 54 ### Props 55 56 #### `children` (required) 57 58 Layout components should accept and use a `children` prop. During rendering, `children` will be populated with the route segments the layout is wrapping. These will primarily be the component of a child [Layout](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page) (if it exists) or [Page](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page), but could also be other special files like [Loading](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading) or [Error](/docs/app/getting-started/error-handling) when applicable. 59 60 #### `params` (optional) 61 62 A promise that resolves to an object containing the [dynamic route parameters](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) object from the root segment down to that layout. 63 64 ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/[team]/layout.tsx" switcher 65 export default async function Layout({ 66 children, 67 params, 68 }: { 69 children: React.ReactNode 70 params: Promise<{ team: string }> 71 }) { 72 const { team } = await params 73 } 74 ``` 75 76 ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/[team]/layout.js" switcher 77 export default async function Layout({ children, params }) { 78 const { team } = await params 79 } 80 ``` 81 82 | Example Route | URL | `params` | 83 | --------------------------------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------- | 84 | `app/dashboard/[team]/layout.js` | `/dashboard/1` | `Promise<{ team: '1' }>` | 85 | `app/shop/[tag]/[item]/layout.js` | `/shop/1/2` | `Promise<{ tag: '1', item: '2' }>` | 86 | `app/blog/[...slug]/layout.js` | `/blog/1/2` | `Promise<{ slug: ['1', '2'] }>` | 87 88 - Since the `params` prop is a promise. You must use `async/await` or React's [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) function to access the values. 89 - In version 14 and earlier, `params` was a synchronous prop. To help with backwards compatibility, you can still access it synchronously in Next.js 15, but this behavior will be deprecated in the future. 90 91 ### Layout Props Helper 92 93 You can type layouts with `LayoutProps` to get a strongly typed `params` and named slots inferred from your directory structure. `LayoutProps` is a globally available helper. 94 95 ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.tsx" 96 export default function Layout(props: LayoutProps<'/dashboard'>) { 97 return ( 98
99 {props.children} 100 {/* If you have app/dashboard/@analytics, it appears as a typed slot: */} 101 {/* {props.analytics} */} 102
103 ) 104 } 105 ``` 106 107 > **Good to know**: 108 > 109 > - Types are generated during `next dev`, `next build` or `next typegen`. 110 > - After type generation, the `LayoutProps` helper is globally available. It doesn't need to be imported. 111 112 ### Root Layout 113 114 The `app` directory **must** include a **root layout**, which is the top-most layout in the root `app` directory. Typically, the root layout is `app/layout.js`. 115 116 ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher 117 export default function RootLayout({ 118 children, 119 }: { 120 children: React.ReactNode 121 }) { 122 return ( 123 124 {children} 125 126 ) 127 } 128 ``` 129 130 ```jsx filename="app/layout.js" switcher 131 export default function RootLayout({ children }) { 132 return ( 133 134 {children} 135 136 ) 137 } 138 ``` 139 140 - The root layout **must** define `` and `` tags. 141 - You should **not** manually add `` tags such as `` and `<meta>` to root layouts. Instead, you should use the [Metadata API](/docs/app/getting-started/metadata-and-og-images) which automatically handles advanced requirements such as streaming and de-duplicating `<head>` elements. 142 - You can create **multiple root layouts**. Any layout without a `layout.js` above it is a root layout. Two common approaches: 143 - Using [route groups](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-groups) like `app/(shop)/layout.js` and `app/(marketing)/layout.js` 144 - Omitting `app/layout.js` so layouts in subdirectories like `app/dashboard/layout.js` and `app/blog/layout.js` each become root layouts for their respective directories. 145 - Navigating **across multiple root layouts** will cause a **full page load** (as opposed to a client-side navigation). 146 - The root layout can be under a **dynamic segment**, for example when implementing [internationalization](/docs/app/guides/internationalization) with `app/[lang]/layout.js`. Dynamic segments before the root layout are **root parameters** and can be read from any Server Component with [`next/root-params`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-root-params). 147 148 ## Caveats 149 150 ### Request Object 151 152 Layouts are cached in the client during navigation to avoid unnecessary server requests. 153 154 [Layouts](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout) do not rerender. They can be cached and reused to avoid unnecessary computation when navigating between pages. By restricting layouts from accessing the raw request, Next.js can prevent the execution of potentially slow or expensive user code within the layout, which could negatively impact performance. 155 156 To access the request object, you can use [`headers`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers) and [`cookies`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) APIs in [Server Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components) and Functions. 157 158 ```tsx filename="app/shop/layout.tsx" switcher 159 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 160 161 export default async function Layout({ children }) { 162 const cookieStore = await cookies() 163 const theme = cookieStore.get('theme') 164 return '...' 165 } 166 ``` 167 168 ```jsx filename="app/shop/layout.js" switcher 169 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 170 171 export default async function Layout({ children }) { 172 const cookieStore = await cookies() 173 const theme = cookieStore.get('theme') 174 return '...' 175 } 176 ``` 177 178 ### Query params 179 180 Layouts do not rerender on navigation, so they cannot access search params which would otherwise become stale. 181 182 To access updated query parameters, you can use the Page [`searchParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#searchparams-optional) prop, or read them inside a Client Component using the [`useSearchParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-search-params) hook. Since Client Components re-render on navigation, they have access to the latest query parameters. 183 184 ```tsx filename="app/ui/search.tsx" switcher 185 'use client' 186 187 import { useSearchParams } from 'next/navigation' 188 189 export default function Search() { 190 const searchParams = useSearchParams() 191 192 const search = searchParams.get('search') 193 194 return '...' 195 } 196 ``` 197 198 ```jsx filename="app/ui/search.js" switcher 199 'use client' 200 201 import { useSearchParams } from 'next/navigation' 202 203 export default function Search() { 204 const searchParams = useSearchParams() 205 206 const search = searchParams.get('search') 207 208 return '...' 209 } 210 ``` 211 212 ```tsx filename="app/shop/layout.tsx" switcher 213 import Search from '@/app/ui/search' 214 215 export default function Layout({ children }) { 216 return ( 217 <> 218 <Search /> 219 {children} 220 </> 221 ) 222 } 223 ``` 224 225 ```jsx filename="app/shop/layout.js" switcher 226 import Search from '@/app/ui/search' 227 228 export default function Layout({ children }) { 229 return ( 230 <> 231 <Search /> 232 {children} 233 </> 234 ) 235 } 236 ``` 237 238 ### Pathname 239 240 Layouts do not re-render on navigation, so they do not access pathname which would otherwise become stale. 241 242 To access the current pathname, you can read it inside a Client Component using the [`usePathname`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-pathname) hook. Since Client Components re-render during navigation, they have access to the latest pathname. 243 244 ```tsx filename="app/ui/breadcrumbs.tsx" switcher 245 'use client' 246 247 import { usePathname } from 'next/navigation' 248 249 // Simplified breadcrumbs logic 250 export default function Breadcrumbs() { 251 const pathname = usePathname() 252 const segments = pathname.split('/') 253 254 return ( 255 <nav> 256 {segments.map((segment, index) => ( 257 <span key={index}> 258 {' > '} 259 {segment} 260 </span> 261 ))} 262 </nav> 263 ) 264 } 265 ``` 266 267 ```jsx filename="app/ui/breadcrumbs.js" default function Layout({ children }) { 307 return ( 308 <> 309 <Breadcrumbs /> 310 <main>{children}</main> 311 </> 312 ) 313 } 314 ``` 315 316 ### Interaction with `loading.js` 317 318 Because `loading.js` sits below `layout.js` in the [component hierarchy](/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure#component-hierarchy), it cannot show a fallback for uncached or runtime data access in the layout itself, such as calling [`cookies()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies), [`headers()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers), or making uncached fetches. 319 320 The behavior depends on whether [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) is enabled: 321 322 - **Without Cache Components:** The navigation will block until the layout finishes rendering, and the `loading.js` fallback will not be shown. 323 - **With Cache Components:** `loading.js` is treated as a regular `<Suspense>` boundary rather than a special prefetch marker. Uncached or runtime data access in the layout must be explicitly wrapped in its own `<Suspense>` boundary, otherwise Next.js guides you with a build-time error. The static shell streams immediately, and the uncached content swaps in as it resolves. 324 325 In both cases, to ensure instant navigation, either: 326 327 - Wrap runtime data access in your layout in its own `<Suspense>` boundary with a fallback. 328 - Move uncached data fetching from `layout.js` into `page.js` where `loading.js` can show a fallback. 329 330 ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.tsx" switcher highlight={8-10} 331 import { Suspense } from 'react' 332 import { NavSkeleton } from './nav-skeleton' 333 import { DashboardNav } from './dashboard-nav' 334 335 export default function Layout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) { 336 return ( 337 <> 338 <Suspense fallback={<NavSkeleton />}> 339 <DashboardNav /> 340 </Suspense> 341 <main>{children}</main> 342 </> 343 ) 344 } 345 ``` 346 347 ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.js" switcher highlight={8-10} 348 import { Suspense } from 'react' 349 import { NavSkeleton } from './nav-skeleton' 350 import { DashboardNav } from './dashboard-nav' 351 352 export default function Layout({ children }) { 353 return ( 354 <> 355 <Suspense fallback={<NavSkeleton />}> 356 <DashboardNav /> 357 </Suspense> 358 <main>{children}</main> 359 </> 360 ) 361 } 362 ``` 363 364 ### Fetching Data 365 366 Layouts cannot pass data to their `children`. However, you can fetch the same data in a route more than once, and use React [`cache`](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) to dedupe the requests without affecting performance. 367 368 Alternatively, when using [`fetch`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/fetch)in Next.js, requests are automatically deduped. 369 370 ```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" switcher 371 export async function getUser(id: string) { 372 const res = await fetch(`https://.../users/${id}`) 373 return res.json() 374 } 375 ``` 376 377 ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.tsx" switcher 378 import { getUser } from During rendering, `children` will be populated with the route segments the layout is wrapping. These will primarily be the component of a child [Layout](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page) (if it exists) or [Page](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page), but could also be other special files like [Loading](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading) or [Error](/docs/app/getting-started/error-handling) when applicable. 59 60 #### `params` (optional) 61 62 A promise that resolves to an object containing the [dynamic route parameters](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) object from the root segment down to that layout. 63 64 ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/[team]/layout.tsx" switcher 65 export default async function Layout({ 66 children, 67 params, 68 }: { 69 children: React.ReactNode 70 params: Promise<{ team: string }> 71 }) { 72 const { team } = await params 73 } 74 ``` 75 76 ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/[team]/layout.js" switcher 77 export default async function Layout({ children, params }) { 78 const { team } = await params 79 } 80 ``` 81 82 | Example Route | URL | `params` | 83 | --------------------------------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------- | 84 | `app/dashboard/[team]/layout.js` | `/dashboard/1` | `Promise<{ team: '1' }>` | 85 | `app/shop/[tag]/[item]/layout.js` | `/shop/1/2` | `Promise<{ tag: '1', item: '2' }>` | 86 | `app/blog/[...slug]/layout.js` | `/blog/1/2` | `Promise<{ slug: ['1', '2'] }>` | 87 88 - Since the `params` prop is a promise. When an error throws within the boundary, the `error` component shows as the fallback UI. 81 82 89 90 > **Good to know**: 91 > 92 > - The [React DevTools](https://react.dev/learn/react-developer-tools) allow you to toggle error boundaries to test error states. 93 > - If you want errors to bubble up to the parent error boundary, you can `throw` when rendering the `error` component. 94 > - For component-level error recovery that aren't tied to route segments like [`error.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/error), use the [`catchError`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/catchError) function. 95 96 In the [component hierarchy](/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure#component-hierarchy), `error.js` wraps `loading.js`, `not-found.js`, `page.js`, and nested `layout.js` files in a React error boundary. It does **not** wrap the `layout.js` or `template.js` above it in the same segment. To handle errors in the root layout, use [`global-error.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/error#global-error). 97 98 ## Reference 99 100 ### Props 101 102 #### `error` 103 104 An instance of an [`Error`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Error) object forwarded to the `error.js` Client Component. 105 106 > **Good to know:** During development, the `Error` object forwarded to the client will be serialized and include the `message` of the original error for easier debugging. However, **this behavior is different in production** to avoid leaking potentially sensitive details included in the error to the client. 107 108 #### `error.message` 109 110 - Errors forwarded from Client Components show the original `Error` message. 111 - Errors forwarded from Server Components show a generic message with an identifier. This is to prevent leaking sensitive details. You can use the identifier, under `errors.digest`, to match the corresponding server-side logs. 112 113 #### `error.digest` 114 115 An automatically generated hash of the error thrown. It can be used to match the corresponding error in server-side logs. 116 117 #### `retry` 118 119 The cause of an error can sometimes be temporary. In these cases, trying again might resolve the issue. 120 121 An error component can use the `retry()` function to prompt the user to attempt to recover from the error. When executed, the function will try to re-fetch and re-render the error boundary's children. If successful, the fallback error component is replaced with the result of the re-render. 122 123 ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/error.tsx" switcher 124 'use client' // Error boundaries must be Client Components 125 126 export default function Error({ 127 error, 128 retry, 129 }: { 130 error: Error & { digest?: string } 131 retry: () => void 132 }) { 133 return ( 134
135

Something went wrong!

136 137
138 ) 139 } 140 ``` 141 142 ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/error.js" switcher 143 'use client' // Error boundaries must be Client Components 144 145 export default function Error({ error, retry }) { 146 return ( 147
148

Something went wrong!

149 150
151 ) 152 } 153 ``` 154 155 #### `reset` 156 157 In most cases, you should use [`retry()`](#retry) instead. However, if you have a specific reason to clear the error state and re-render the error boundary's children without re-fetching the contents, you can use the `reset()` function. 158 159 ## Examples 160 161 ### Global Error 162 163 While less common, you can handle errors in the root layout or template using `global-error.jsx`, located in the root app directory, even when leveraging [internationalization](/docs/app/guides/internationalization). Global error UI must define its own `` and `` tags, global styles, fonts, or other dependencies that your error page requires. This file replaces the root layout or template when active. 164 165 > **Good to know**: `global-error` and the built-in 500 page render their own document and do **not** include your global styles, so an app-level theme toggle (a class or `data-theme` attribute) won't reach them. The default UI follows the OS color scheme; to match your app's theme, apply it inside your own `global-error` component. 166 167 > **Good to know**: Error boundaries must be [Client Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components#using-client-components), which means that [`metadata` and `generateMetadata`](/docs/app/getting-started/metadata-and-og-images) exports are not supported in `global-error.jsx`. As an alternative, you can use the React [``](https://react.dev/reference/react-dom/components/title) component. 168 169 ```tsx filename="app/global-error.tsx" switcher 170 'use client' // Error boundaries must be Client Components 171 172 export default function GlobalError({ 173 error, 174 retry, 175 }: { 176 error: Error & { digest?: string } 177 retry: () => void 178 }) { 179 return ( 180 // global-error must include html and body tags 181 <html> 182 <body> 183 <h2>Something went wrong!</h2> 184 <button onClick={() => retry()}>Try again</button> 185 </body> 186 </html> 187 ) 188 } 189 ``` 190 191 ```jsx filename="app/global-error.js" switcher 192 'use client' // Error boundaries must be Client Components 193 194 export default function GlobalError({ error, retry }) { 195 return ( 196 // global-error must include html and body tags 197 <html> 198 <body> 199 <h2>Something went wrong!</h2> 200 <button onClick={() => retry()}>Try again</button> 201 </body> 202 </html> 203 ) 204 } 205 ``` 206 207 ### Graceful error recovery with a custom error boundary 208 209 When rendering fails on the client, it can be useful to show the last known server rendered UI for a better user experience. 210 211 The `GracefullyDegradingErrorBoundary` is an example of a custom error boundary that captures and preserves the current HTML before an error occurs. If a rendering error happens, it re-renders the captured HTML and displays a persistent notification bar to inform the user. 212 213 ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/error.tsx" switcher 214 'use client' 215 216 import React, { Component, ErrorInfo, ReactNode } from 'react' 217 218 interface ErrorBoundaryProps { 219 children: ReactNode 220 onError?: (error: Error, errorInfo: ErrorInfo) => void 221 } 222 223 interface ErrorBoundaryState { 224 hasError: boolean 225 } 226 227 export class GracefullyDegradingErrorBoundary extends Component< 228 ErrorBoundaryProps, 229 ErrorBoundaryState 230 > { 231 private contentRef: React.RefObject<HTMLDivElement | null> 232 233 constructor(props: ErrorBoundaryProps) { 234 super(props) 235 this.state = { hasError: false } 236 this.contentRef = 1	---
2	title: generateStaticParams
3	description: API reference for the generateStaticParams function.
4	---
5	
6	The `generateStaticParams` function can be used in combination with [dynamic route segments](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) to [**statically generate**](/docs/app/glossary#prerendering) routes at build time instead of on-demand at request time.
7	
8	`generateStaticParams` can be used with:
9	
10	- [Pages](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page) (`page.tsx`/`page.js`)
11	- [Layouts](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout) (`layout.tsx`/`layout.js`)
12	- [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) (`route.ts`/`route.js`)
13	
14	```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
15	// Return a list of `params` to populate the [slug] dynamic segment
16	export async function generateStaticParams() {
17	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
18	
19	  return posts.map((post) => ({
20	    slug: post.slug,
21	  }))
22	}
23	
24	// Multiple versions of this page will be statically generated
25	// using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
26	export default async function Page({
27	  params,
28	}: {
29	  params: Promise<{ slug: string }>
30	}) {
31	  const { slug } = await params
32	  // ...
33	}
34	```
35	
36	```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
37	// Return a list of `params` to populate the [slug] dynamic segment
38	export async function generateStaticParams() {
39	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
40	
41	  return posts.map((post) => ({
42	    slug: post.slug,
43	  }))
44	}
45	
46	// Multiple versions of this page will be statically generated
47	// using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
48	export default async function Page({ params }) {
49	  const { slug } = await params
50	  // ...
51	}
52	```
53	
54	> **Good to know**:
55	>
56	> - You can use the [`dynamicParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/dynamicParams) segment config option to control what happens when a dynamic segment is visited that was not generated with `generateStaticParams`.
57	> - You must return [an empty array from `generateStaticParams`](#all-paths-at-runtime) or utilize [`export const dynamic = 'force-static'`](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#dynamic) in order to revalidate (ISR) [paths at runtime](#all-paths-at-runtime).
58	> - During `next dev`, `generateStaticParams` will be called when you navigate to a route.
59	> - During `next build`, `generateStaticParams` runs before the corresponding Layouts or Pages are generated.
60	> - During revalidation (ISR), `generateStaticParams` will not be called again.
61	> - `generateStaticParams` replaces the [`getStaticPaths`](/docs/pages/api-reference/functions/get-static-paths) function in the Pages Router.
62	
63	## Parameters
64	
65	`options.params` (optional)
66	
67	If multiple dynamic segments in a route use `generateStaticParams`, the child `generateStaticParams` function is executed once for each set of `params` the parent generates.
68	
69	The `params` object contains the populated `params` from the parent `generateStaticParams`, which can be used to [generate the `params` in a child segment](#multiple-dynamic-segments-in-a-route).
70	
71	## Returns
72	
73	`generateStaticParams` should return an array of objects where each object represents the populated dynamic segments of a single route.
74	
75	- Each property in the object is a dynamic segment to be filled in for the route.
76	- The properties name is the segment's name, and the properties value is what that segment should be filled in with.
77	
78	| Example Route                    | `generateStaticParams` Return Type        |
79	| -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
80	| `/product/[id]`                  | `{ id: string }[]`                        |
81	| `/products/[category]/[product]` | `{ category: string, product: string }[]` |
82	| `/products/[...slug]`            | `{ slug: string[] }[]`                    |
83	
84	## Single Dynamic Segment
85	
86	```tsx filename="app/product/[id]/page.tsx" switcher
87	export function generateStaticParams() {
88	  return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
89	}
90	
91	// Three versions of this page will be statically generated
92	// using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
93	// - /product/1
94	// - /product/2
95	// - /product/3
96	export default async function Page({
97	  params,
98	}: {
99	  params: Promise<{ id: string }>
100	}) {
101	  const { id } = await params
102	  // ...
103	}
104	```
105	
106	```jsx filename="app/product/[id]/page.js" switcher
107	export function generateStaticParams() {
108	  return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
109	}
110	
111	// Three versions of this page will be statically generated
112	// using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
113	// - /product/1
114	// - /product/2
115	// - /product/3
116	export default async function Page({ params }) {
117	  const { id } = await params
118	  // ...
119	}
120	```
121	
122	## Multiple Dynamic Segments
123	
124	```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
125	export function generateStaticParams() {
126	  return [
127	    { category: 'a', product: '1' },
128	    { category: 'b', product: '2' },
129	    { category: 'c', product: '3' },
130	  ]
131	}
132	
133	// Three versions of this page will be statically generated
134	// using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
135	// - /products/a/1
136	// - /products/b/2
137	// - /products/c/3
138	export default async function Page({
139	  params,
140	}: {
141	  params: Promise<{ category: string; product: string }>
142	}) {
143	  const { category, product } = await params
144	  // ...
145	}
146	```
147	
148	```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js" switcher
149	export function generateStaticParams() {
150	  return [
151	    { category: 'a', product: '1' },
152	    { category: 'b', product: '2' },
153	    { category: 'c', product: '3' },
154	  ]
155	}
156	
157	// Three versions of this page will be statically generated
158	// using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
159	// - /products/a/1
160	// - /products/b/2
161	// - /products/c/3
162	export default async function Page({ params }) {
163	  const { category, product } = await params
164	  // ...
165	}
166	```
167	
168	## Catch-all Dynamic Segment
169	
170	```tsx filename="app/product/[...slug]/page.tsx" switcher
171	export function generateStaticParams() {
172	  return [{ slug: ['a', '1'] }, { slug: ['b', '2'] }, { slug: ['c', '3'] }]
173	}
174	
175	// Three versions of this page will be statically generated
176	// using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
177	// - /product/a/1
178	// - /product/b/2
179	// - /product/c/3
180	export default async function Page({
181	  params,
182	}: {
183	  params: Promise<{ slug: string[] }>
184	}) {
185	  const { slug } = await params
186	  // ...
187	}
188	```
189	
190	```jsx filename="app/product/[...slug]/page.js" switcher
191	export function generateStaticParams() {
192	  return [{ slug: ['a', '1'] }, { slug: ['b', '2'] }, { slug: ['c', '3'] }]
193	}
194	
195	// Three versions of this page will be statically generated
196	// using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
197	// - /product/a/1
198	// - /product/b/2
199	// - /product/c/3
200	export default async function Page({ params }) {
201	  const { slug } = await params
202	  // ...
203	}
204	```
205	
206	## Examples
207	
208	### Prerendering
209	
210	#### All paths at build time
211	
212	To statically render all paths at build time, supply the full list of paths to `generateStaticParams`:
213	
214	```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
215	export async function generateStaticParams() {
216	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
217	
218	  return posts.map((post) => ({
219	    slug: post.slug,
220	  }))
221	}
222	```
223	
224	```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
225	export async function generateStaticParams() {
226	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
227	
228	  return posts.map((post) => ({
229	    slug: post.slug,
230	  }))
231	}
232	```
233	
234	#### Subset of paths at build time
235	
236	To statically render a subset of paths at build time, and the rest the first time they're visited at runtime, return a partial list of paths:
237	
238	```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
239	export async function generateStaticParams() {
240	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
241	
242	  // Render the first 10 posts at build time
243	  return posts.slice(0, 10).map((post) => ({
244	    slug: post.slug,
245	  }))
246	}
247	```
248	
249	```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
250	export async function generateStaticParams() {
251	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
252	
253	  // Render the first 10 posts at build time
254	  return posts.slice(0, 10).map((post) => ({
255	    slug: post.slug,
256	  }))
257	}
258	```
259	
260	Then, by using the [`dynamicParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/dynamicParams) segment config option, you can control what happens when a dynamic segment is visited that was not generated with `generateStaticParams`.
261	
262	```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
263	// All posts besides the top 10 will be a 404
264	export const dynamicParams = false
265	
266	export async function generateStaticParams() {
267	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
268	  const topPosts = posts.slice(0, 10)
269	
270	  return topPosts.map((post) => ({
271	    slug: post.slug,
272	  }))
273	}
274	```
275	
276	```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
277	// All posts besides the top 10 will be a 404
278	export const dynamicParams = false
279	
280	export async function generateStaticParams() {
281	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
282	  const topPosts = posts.slice(0, 10)
283	
284	  return topPosts.map((post) => ({
285	    slug: post.slug,
286	  }))
287	}
288	```
289	
290	#### All paths at runtime
291	
292	To statically render all paths the first time they're visited, return an empty array (no paths will be rendered at build time) or utilize [`export const dynamic = 'force-static'`](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#dynamic):
293	
294	```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js"
295	export async function generateStaticParams() {
296	  return []
297	}
298	```
299	
300	> **Good to know:**
301	>
302	> - You must always return an array from `generateStaticParams`, even if it's empty. Otherwise, the route will be dynamically rendered.
303	
304	```jsx filename="app/changelog/[slug]/page.js"
305	export const dynamic = 'force-static'
306	```
307	
308	#### With Cache Components
309	
310	When using [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) with dynamic routes, `generateStaticParams` must return **at least one param**. Empty arrays cause a [build error](/docs/messages/empty-generate-static-params). This allows Cache Components to validate your route doesn't incorrectly access `cookies()`, `headers()`, or `searchParams` at runtime.
311	
312	> **Good to know**: If you don't know the actual param values at build time, you can return a placeholder param (e.g., `[{ slug: '__placeholder__' }]`) for validation, then handle it in your page with `notFound()`. However, this prevents build time validation from working effectively and may cause runtime errors.
313	
314	See the [dynamic routes section](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes#with-cache-components) for detailed walkthroughs, or [ISR with Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components) for prerendering a subset of routes and serving App Shells for the rest.
315	
316	### With Route Handlers
317	
318	You can use `generateStaticParams` with [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) to statically generate API responses at build time:
319	
320	```ts filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts" switcher
321	export async function generateStaticParams() {
322	  return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
323	}
324	
325	export async function GET(
326	  request: Request,
327	  { params }: RouteContext<'/api/posts/[id]'>
328	) {
329	  const { id } = await params
330	  // This will be statically generated for IDs 1, 2, and 3
331	  return Response.json({ id, title: `Post ${id}` })
332	}
333	```
334	
335	```js filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.js" switcher
336	export async function generateStaticParams() {
337	  return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
338	}
339	
340	export async function GET(request, { params }) {
341	  const { id } = await params
342	  // This will be statically generated for IDs 1, 2, and 3
343	  return Response.json({ id, title: `Post ${id}` })
344	}
345	```
346	
347	### Route Handlers with Cache Components
348	
349	When using [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching), combine with `use cache` for optimal caching:
350	
351	```ts filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts"
352	export async function generateStaticParams() {
353	  return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
354	}
355	
356	async function getPost(id: Promise<string>) {
357	  'use cache'
358	  const resolvedId = await id
359	  const response = await fetch(`https://api.example.com/posts/${resolvedId}`)
360	  return response.json()
361	}
362	
363	export async function GET(
364	  request: Request,
365	  { params }: RouteContext<'/api/posts/[id]'>
366	) {
367	  const post = await getPost(params.then((p) => p.id))
368	  return Response.json(post)
369	}
370	```
371	
372	See the [Route Handlers documentation](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route#static-generation-with-generatestaticparams) for more details.
373	
374	### Disable rendering for unspecified paths
375	
376	To prevent unspecified paths from being prerendered at runtime, add the `export const dynamicParams = false` option in a route segment. When this config option is used, only paths provided by `generateStaticParams` will be served, and unspecified routes will 404 or match (in the case of [catch-all routes](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes#catch-all-segments)).
377	
378	### Multiple Dynamic Segments in a Route
379	
380	You can generate params for dynamic segments above the current layout or page, but **not below**. For example, given the `app/products/[category]/[product]` route:
381	
382	- `app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js` can generate params for **both** `[category]` and `[product]`.
383	- `app/products/[category]/layout.js` can **only** generate params for `[category]`.
384	
385	There are two approaches to generating params for a route with multiple dynamic segments:
386	
387	#### Generate params from the bottom up
388	
389	Generate multiple dynamic segments from the child route segment.
390	
391	```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
392	// Generate segments for both [category] and [product]
393	export async function generateStaticParams() {
394	  const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
395	
396	  return products.map((product) => ({
397	    category: product.category.slug,
398	    product: product.id,
399	  }))
400	}
401	
402	export default function Page({
403	  params,
404	}: {
405	  params: Promise<{ category: string; product: string }>
406	}) {
407	  // ...
408	}
409	```
410	
411	```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js" switcher
412	// Generate segments for both [category] and [product]
413	export async function generateStaticParams() {
414	  const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
415	
416	  return products.map((product) => ({
417	    category: product.category.slug,
418	    product: product.id,
419	  }))
420	}
421	
422	export default function Page({ params }) {
423	  // ...
424	}
425	```
426	
427	#### Generate params from the top down
428	
429	Generate the parent segments first and use the result to generate the child segments.
430	
431	```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/layout.tsx" switcher
432	// Generate segments for [category]
433	export async function generateStaticParams() {
434	  const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
435	
436	  return products.map((product) => ({
437	    category: product.category.slug,
438	  }))
439	}
440	
441	export default function Layout({
442	  params,
443	}: {
444	  params: Promise<{ category: string }>
445	}) {
446	  // ...
447	}
448	```
449	
450	```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/layout.js" switcher
451	// Generate segments for [category]
452	export async function generateStaticParams() {
453	  const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
454	
455	  return products.map((product) => ({
456	    category: product.category.slug,
457	  }))
458	}
459	
460	export default function Layout({ params }) {
461	  // ...
462	}
463	```
464	
465	A child route segment's `generateStaticParams` function is executed once for each segment a parent `generateStaticParams` generates.
466	
467	The child `generateStaticParams` function can use the `params` returned from the parent `generateStaticParams` function to dynamically generate its own segments.
468	
469	```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
470	// Generate segments for [product] using the `params` passed from
471	// the parent segment's `generateStaticParams` function
472	export async function generateStaticParams({
473	  params: { category },
474	}: {
475	  params: { category: string }
476	}) {
477	  const products = await fetch(
478	    `https://.../products?category=${category}`
479	  ).then((res) => res.json())
480	
481	  return products.map((product) => ({
482	    product: product.id,
483	  }))
484	}
485	
486	export default function Page({
487	  params,
488	}: {
489	  params: Promise<{ category: string; product: string }>
490	}) {
491	  // ...
492	}
493	```
494	
495	```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js" switcher
496	// Generate segments for [product] using the `params` passed from
497	// the parent segment's `generateStaticParams` function
498	export async function generateStaticParams({ params: { category } }) {
499	  const products = await fetch(
500	    `https://.../products?category=${category}`
501	  ).then((res) => res.json())
502	
503	  return products.map((product) => ({
504	    product: product.id,
505	  }))
506	}
507	
508	export default function Page({ params }) {
509	  // ...
510	}
511	```
512	
513	Notice that the params argument can be accessed synchronously and includes only parent segment params.
514	
515	> **Good to know:** When a parent dynamic segment is a [root parameter](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-root-params), you can also read it inside a nested `generateStaticParams` by calling its getter from the `next/root-params` module.
516	
517	For type completion, you can make use of the TypeScript `Awaited` helper in combination with either [`Page Props helper`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#page-props-helper) or [`Layout Props helper`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout#layout-props-helper):
518	
519	```ts filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
520	export async function generateStaticParams({
521	  params: { category },
522	}: {
523	  params: Awaited<LayoutProps<'/products/[category]'>['params']>
524	}) {
525	  const products = await fetch(
526	    `https://.../products?category=${category}`
527	  ).then((res) => res.json())
528	
529	  return products.map((product) => ({
530	    product: product.id,
531	  }))
532	}
533	```
534	
535	> **Good to know**: `fetch` requests are automatically [memoized](/docs/app/glossary#memoization) for the same data across all `generate`-prefixed functions, Layouts, Pages, and Server Components. React [`cache` can be used](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) if `fetch` is unavailable.
536	
537	## Version History
538	
539	| Version   | Changes                            |
540	| --------- | ---------------------------------- |
541	| `v13.0.0` | `generateStaticParams` introduced. |
542

4	---
5	
6	The `generateStaticParams` function can be used in combination with [dynamic route segments](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) to [**statically generate**](/docs/app/glossary#prerendering) routes at build time instead of on-demand at request time.
7	
8	`generateStaticParams` can be used with:
9	
10	- [Pages](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page) (`page.tsx`/`page.js`)
11	- [Layouts](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout) (`layout.tsx`/`layout.js`)
12	- [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) (`route.ts`/`route.js`)
13	
14	```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
15	// Return a list of `params` to populate the [slug] dynamic segment
16	export async function generateStaticParams() {
17	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
18	
19	  return posts.map((post) => ({
20	    slug: post.slug,
21	  }))
22	}
23	
24	// Multiple versions of this page will be statically generated
25	// using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
26	export default async function Page({
27	  params,
28	}: {
29	  params: Promise<{ slug: string }>
30	}) {
31	  const { slug } = await params
32	  // ...
33	}
34	```
35	
36	```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
37	// Return a list of `params` to populate the [slug] dynamic segment
38	export async function generateStaticParams() {
39	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
40	
41	  return posts.map((post) => ({
42	    slug: post.slug,
43	  }))
44	}
45	
46	// Multiple versions of this page will be statically generated
47	// using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
48	export default async function Page({ params }) {
49	  const { slug } = await params
50	  // ...
51	}
52	```
53	
54	> **Good to know**:
55	>
56	> - You can use the [`dynamicParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/dynamicParams) segment config option to control what happens when a dynamic segment is visited that was not generated with `generateStaticParams`.
57	> - You must return [an empty array from `generateStaticParams`](#all-paths-at-runtime) or utilize [`export const dynamic = 'force-static'`](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#dynamic) in order to revalidate (ISR) [paths at runtime](#all-paths-at-runtime).
58	> - During `next dev`, `generateStaticParams` will be called when you navigate to a route.
59	> - During `next build`, `generateStaticParams` runs before the corresponding Layouts or Pages are generated.
60	> - During revalidation (ISR), `generateStaticParams` will not be called again.
61	> - `generateStaticParams` replaces the [`getStaticPaths`](/docs/pages/api-reference/functions/get-static-paths) function in the Pages Router.
62	
63	## Parameters
64	
65	`options.params` (optional)
66	
67	If multiple dynamic segments in a route use `generateStaticParams`, the child `generateStaticParams` function is executed once for each set of `params` the parent generates.
68	
69	The `params` object contains the populated `params` from the parent `generateStaticParams`, which can be used to [generate the `params` in a child segment](#multiple-dynamic-segments-in-a-route).
70	
71	## Returns
72	
73	`generateStaticParams` should return an array of objects where each object represents the populated dynamic segments of a single route.
74	
75	- Each property in the object is a dynamic segment to be filled in for the route.
76	- The properties name is the segment's name, and the properties value is what that segment should be filled in with.
77	
78	| Example Route                    | `generateStaticParams` Return Type        |
79	| -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
80	| `/product/[id]`                  | `{ id: string }[]`                        |
81	| `/products/[category]/[product]` | `{ category: string, product: string }[]` |
82	| `/products/[...slug]`            | `{ slug: string[] }[]`                    |

206	## Examples
207	
208	### Prerendering
209	
210	#### All paths at build time
211	
212	To statically render all paths at build time, supply the full list of paths to `generateStaticParams`:
213	
214	```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
215	export async function generateStaticParams() {
216	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
217	
218	  return posts.map((post) => ({
219	    slug: post.slug,
220	  }))
221	}
222	```
223	
224	```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
225	export async function generateStaticParams() {
226	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
227	
228	  return posts.map((post) => ({
229	    slug: post.slug,
230	  }))
231	}
232	```
233	
234	#### Subset of paths at build time
235	
236	To statically render a subset of paths at build time, and the rest the first time they're visited at runtime, return a partial list of paths:
237	
238	```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
239	export async function generateStaticParams() {
240	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
241	
242	  // Render the first 10 posts at build time
243	  return posts.slice(0, 10).map((post) => ({
244	    slug: post.slug,
245	  }))
246	}
247	```

251	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
252

254	  return posts.slice(0, 10).map((post) => ({
255	    slug: post.slug,
256	  }))
257	}
258	```

260	Then, by using the [`dynamicParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/dynamicParams) segment config option, you can control what happens when a dynamic segment is visited that was not generated with `generateStaticParams`.
261	
262	```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
263	// All posts besides the top 10 will be a 404
264	export const dynamicParams = false
265	
266	export async function generateStaticParams() {
267	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
268	  const topPosts = posts.slice(0, 10)
269	
270	  return topPosts.map((post) => ({
271	    slug: post.slug,
272	  }))
273	}
274	```

283

290	#### All paths at runtime
291	
292	To statically render all paths the first time they're visited, return an empty array (no paths will be rendered at build time) or utilize [`export const dynamic = 'force-static'`](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#dynamic):
293	
294	```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js"
295	export async function generateStaticParams() {
296	  return []
297	}
298	```
299	
300	> **Good to know:**
301	>
302	> - You must always return an array from `generateStaticParams`, even if it's empty. Otherwise, the route will be dynamically rendered.
303	
304	```jsx filename="app/changelog/[slug]/page.js"
305	export const dynamic = 'force-static'
306	```
307	
308	#### With Cache Components
309	
310	When using [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) with dynamic routes, `generateStaticParams` must return **at least one param**. Empty arrays cause a [build error](/docs/messages/empty-generate-static-params). This allows Cache Components to validate your route doesn't incorrectly access `cookies()`, `headers()`, or `searchParams` at runtime.
311	
312	> **Good to know**: If you don't know the actual param values at build time, you can return a placeholder param (e.g., `[{ slug: '__placeholder__' }]`) for validation, then handle it in your page with `notFound()`. However, this prevents build time validation from working effectively and may cause runtime errors.
313	
314	See the [dynamic routes section](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes#with-cache-components) for detailed walkthroughs, or [ISR with Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components) for prerendering a subset of routes and serving App Shells for the rest.
315	
316	### With Route Handlers
317	
318	You can use `generateStaticParams` with [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) to statically generate API responses at build time:
319	
320	```ts filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts" switcher
321	export async function generateStaticParams() {
322	  return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
323	}
324	
325	export async function GET(
326	  request: Request,
327	  { params }: RouteContext<'/api/posts/[id]'>
328	) {
329	  const { id } = await params
330	  // This will be statically generated for IDs 1, 2, and 3
331	  return Response.json({ id, title: `Post ${id}` })
332	}
333	```

335	```js filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.js" switcher

344	}
345	```

347	### Route Handlers with Cache Components
348	
349	When using [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching), combine with `use cache` for optimal caching:
350	
351	```ts filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts"

353	  return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
354	}

356	async function getPost(id: Promise<string>) {
357	  'use cache'
358	  const resolvedId = await id
359	  const response = await fetch(`https://api.example.com/posts/${resolvedId}`)
360	  return response.json()
361	}
362	
363	export async function GET(
364	  request: Request,
365	  { params }: RouteContext<'/api/posts/[id]'>
366	) {
367	  const post = await getPost(params.then((p) => p.id))
368	  return Response.json(post)
369	}
370	```

476	}) {
477	  const products = await fetch(
478	    `https://.../products?category=${category}`
479	  ).then((res) => res.json())
480	
481	  return products.map((product) => ({
482	    product: product.id,
483	  }))
484	}
485	
486	export default function Page({
487	  params,
488	}: {
489	  params: Promise<{ category: string; product: string }>
490	}) {
491	  // ...
492	}
493	```
494	
495	```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js" switcher
496	// Generate segments for [product] using the `params` passed from
497	// the parent segment's `generateStaticParams` function
498	export async function generateStaticParams({ params: { category } }) {
499	  const products = await fetch(
500	    `https://.../products?category=${category}`
501	  ).then((res) => res.json())
502	
503	  return products.map((product) => ({
504	    product: product.id,
505	  }))
506	}
507	
508	export default function Page({ params }) {
509	  // ...
510	}
511	```
512	
513	Notice that the params argument can be accessed synchronously and includes only parent segment params.
514	
515	> **Good to know:** When a parent dynamic segment is a [root parameter](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-root-params), you can also read it inside a nested `generateStaticParams` by calling its getter from the `next/root-params` module.
516	
517	For type completion, you can make use of the TypeScript `Awaited` helper in combination with either [`Page Props helper`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#page-props-helper) or [`Layout Props helper`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout#layout-props-helper):
518	
519	```ts filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
520	export async function generateStaticParams({
521	  params: { category },
522	}: {
523	  params: Awaited<LayoutProps<'/products/[category]'>['params']>
524	}) {
525	  const products = await fetch(
526	    `https://.../products?category=${category}`
527	  ).then((res) => res.json())
528	
529	  return products.map((product) => ({
530	    product: product.id,
531	  }))
532	}
533	```
534	
535	> **Good to know**: `fetch` requests are automatically [memoized](/docs/app/glossary#memoization) for the same data across all `generate`-prefixed functions, Layouts, Pages, and Server Components. React [`cache` can be used](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) if `fetch` is unavailable.
536	
537	## Version History
538	
539	| Version   | Changes                            |
540	| --------- | ---------------------------------- |
541	| `v13.0.0` | `generateStaticParams` introduced. |

1	---
2	title: Caching and Revalidating (Previous Model)
3	nav_title: Caching (Previous Model)
4	description: Learn how to cache and revalidate data using fetch options, unstable_cache, and route segment configs for projects not using Cache Components.
5	---
6	
7	> This guide assumes you are **not** using [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) which was introduced in version 16 under the [`cacheComponents` flag](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents).
8	
9	## Caching `fetch` requests
10	
11	By default, [`fetch`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/fetch) requests are not cached. You can cache individual requests by setting the `cache` option to `'force-cache'`.
12	
13	```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
14	export default async function Page() {
15	  const data = await fetch('https://...', { cache: 'force-cache' })
16	}
17	```
18	
19	```jsx filename="app/page.jsx" switcher
20	export default async function Page() {
21	  const data = await fetch('https://...', { cache: 'force-cache' })
22	}
23	```
24	
25	See the [`fetch` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/fetch) to learn more.
26	
27	### `unstable_cache` for non-`fetch` functions
28	
29	`unstable_cache` allows you to cache the result of database queries and other async functions that don't use `fetch`. Wrap `unstable_cache` around the function:
30	
31	```ts filename="app/lib/data.ts" switcher
32	import { unstable_cache } from 'next/cache'
33	import { db } from '@/lib/db'
34	
35	export const getCachedUser = unstable_cache(
36	  async (id: string) => {
37	    return db
38	      .select()
39	      .from(users)
40	      .where(eq(users.id, id))
41	      .then((res) => res[0])
42	  },
43	  ['user'], // cache key prefix
44	  {
45	    tags: ['user'],
46	    revalidate: 3600,
47	  }
48	)
49	```
50	
51	```js filename="app/lib/data.js" switcher
52	import { unstable_cache } from 'next/cache'
53	import { db } from '@/lib/db'
54	
55	export const getCachedUser = unstable_cache(
56	  async (id) => {
57	    return db
58	      .select()
59	      .from(users)
60	      .where(eq(users.id, id))
61	      .then((res) => res[0])
62	  },
63	  ['user'], // cache key prefix
64	  {
65	    tags: ['user'],
66	    revalidate: 3600,
67	  }
68	)
69	```
70	
71	The third argument accepts:
72	
73	- `tags`: an array of tags for on-demand revalidation with `revalidateTag`.
74	- `revalidate`: the number of seconds before the cache is revalidated.
75	
76	See the [`unstable_cache` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/unstable_cache) to learn more.
77	
78	### Route segment config
79	
80	You can configure caching behavior at the route level by exporting config options from a [Page](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page), [Layout](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout), or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route).
81	
82	#### `dynamic`
83	
84	Change the dynamic behavior of a layout or page to fully static or fully dynamic.
85	
86	```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx | route.ts" switcher
87	export const dynamic = 'auto'
88	// 'auto' | 'force-dynamic' | 'error' | 'force-static'
89	```
90	
91	```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js | route.js" switcher
92	export const dynamic = 'auto'
93	// 'auto' | 'force-dynamic' | 'error' | 'force-static'
94	```
95	
96	- **`'auto'`** (default): The default option to cache as much as possible without preventing any components from opting into dynamic behavior.
97	- **`'force-dynamic'`**: Force [dynamic rendering](/docs/app/glossary#dynamic-rendering), which will result in routes being rendered for each user at request time. This option is equivalent to:
98	  - Setting the option of every `fetch()` request in a layout or page to `{ cache: 'no-store', next: { revalidate: 0 } }`.
99	  - Setting the segment config to `export const fetchCache = 'force-no-store'`
100	- **`'error'`**: Force prerendering and cache the data of a layout or page by causing an error if any components use Request-time APIs or uncached data. This option is equivalent to:
101	  - `getStaticProps()` in the `pages` directory.
102	  - Setting the option of every `fetch()` request in a layout or page to `{ cache: 'force-cache' }`.
103	  - Setting the segment config to `fetchCache = 'only-cache'`.
104	- **`'force-static'`**: Force prerendering and cache the data of a layout or page by forcing [`cookies`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies), [`headers()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers) and [`useSearchParams()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-search-params) to return empty values. It is possible to [`revalidate`](#route-segment-config-revalidate), [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath), or [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag), in pages or layouts rendered with `force-static`.
105	
106	#### `fetchCache`
107	
108	<details>
109	  <summary>This is an advanced option that should only be used if you specifically need to override the default behavior.</summary>
110	
111	A `fetch` request that sets no `cache` option is fetched once during `next build` if it is reachable **before** any Request-time APIs are used, because the route is prerendered up to that point. Requests discovered **after** a Request-time API run on every request.
112	
113	`fetchCache` allows you to override the default `cache` option of all `fetch` requests in a layout or page.
114	
115	```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx | route.ts" switcher
116	export const fetchCache = 'auto'
117	// 'auto' | 'default-cache' | 'only-cache'
118	// 'force-cache' | 'force-no-store' | 'default-no-store' | 'only-no-store'
119	```
120	
121	```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js | route.js" switcher
122	export const fetchCache = 'auto'
123	// 'auto' | 'default-cache' | 'only-cache'
124	// 'force-cache' | 'force-no-store' | 'default-no-store' | 'only-no-store'
125	```
126	
127	- **`'auto'`** (default): The default option to cache `fetch` requests before Request-time APIs with the `cache` option they provide and not cache `fetch` requests after Request-time APIs.
128	- **`'default-cache'`**: Allow any `cache` option to be passed to `fetch` but if no option is provided then set the `cache` option to `'force-cache'`. This means that even `fetch` requests after Request-time APIs are considered static.
129	- **`'only-cache'`**: Ensure all `fetch` requests opt into caching by changing the default to `cache: 'force-cache'` if no option is provided and causing an error if any `fetch` requests use `cache: 'no-store'`.
130	- **`'force-cache'`**: Ensure all `fetch` requests opt into caching by setting the `cache` option of all `fetch` requests to `'force-cache'`.
131	- **`'default-no-store'`**: Allow any `cache` option to be passed to `fetch` but if no option is provided then set the `cache` option to `'no-store'`. This means that even `fetch` requests before Request-time APIs are considered dynamic.
132	- **`'only-no-store'`**: Ensure all `fetch` requests opt out of caching by changing the default to `cache: 'no-store'` if no option is provided and causing an error if any `fetch` requests use `cache: 'force-cache'`
133	- **`'force-no-store'`**: Ensure all `fetch` requests opt out of caching by setting the `cache` option of all `fetch` requests to `'no-store'`. This forces all `fetch` requests to be re-fetched every request even if they provide a `'force-cache'` option.
134	
135	##### Cross-route segment behavior
136	
137	- Any options set across each layout and page of a single route need to be compatible with each other.
138	  - If both the `'only-cache'` and `'force-cache'` are provided, then `'force-cache'` wins. If both `'only-no-store'` and `'force-no-store'` are provided, then `'force-no-store'` wins. The force option changes the behavior across the route so a single segment with `'force-*'` would prevent any errors caused by `'only-*'`.
139	  - The intention of the `'only-*'` and `'force-*'` options is to guarantee the whole route is either fully static or fully dynamic. This means:
140	    - A combination of `'only-cache'` and `'only-no-store'` in a single route is not allowed.
141	    - A combination of `'force-cache'` and `'force-no-store'` in a single route is not allowed.
142	  - A parent cannot provide `'default-no-store'` if a child provides `'auto'` or `'*-cache'` since that could make the same fetch have different behavior.
143	- It is generally recommended to leave shared parent layouts as `'auto'` and customize the options where child segments diverge.
144	
145	</details>
146	
147	## Time-based revalidation
148	
149	Use the `next.revalidate` option on `fetch` to revalidate data after a specified number of seconds:
150	
151	```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
152	export default async function Page() {
153	  const data = await fetch('https://...', { next: { revalidate: 3600 } })
154	}
155	```
156	
157	```jsx filename="app/page.jsx" switcher
158	export default async function Page() {
159	  const data = await fetch('https://...', { next: { revalidate: 3600 } })
160	}
161	```
162	
163	For non-`fetch` functions, `unstable_cache` accepts a `revalidate` option in its configuration (see [example above](#unstable_cache-for-non-fetch-functions)).
164	
165	### Route segment config `revalidate`
166	
167	Set the default revalidation time for a layout or page. This option does not override the `revalidate` value set by individual `fetch` requests.
168	
169	```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx | route.ts" switcher
170	export const revalidate = false
171	// false | 0 | number
172	```
173	
174	```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js | route.js" switcher
175	export const revalidate = false
176	// false | 0 | number
177	```
178	
179	- **`false`** (default): The default heuristic to cache any `fetch` requests that set their `cache` option to `'force-cache'` or are discovered before a Request-time API is used. Semantically equivalent to `revalidate: Infinity` which effectively means the resource should be cached indefinitely. It is still possible for individual `fetch` requests to use `cache: 'no-store'` or `revalidate: 0` to avoid being cached and make the route dynamically rendered. Or set `revalidate` to a positive number lower than the route default to increase the revalidation frequency of a route.
180	- **`0`**: Ensure a layout or page is always dynamically rendered even if no Request-time APIs or uncached data fetches are discovered. This option changes the default of `fetch` requests that do not set a `cache` option to `'no-store'` but leaves `fetch` requests that opt into `'force-cache'` or use a positive `revalidate` as is.
181	- **`number`**: (in seconds) Set the default revalidation frequency of a layout or page to `n` seconds.
182	
183	> **Good to know**:
184	>
185	> - The revalidate value needs to be statically analyzable. For example `revalidate = 600` is valid, but `revalidate = 60 * 10` is not.
186	> - The revalidate value is not available when using the deprecated `runtime = 'edge'`.
187	> - In Development, Pages are _always_ rendered on-demand and are never cached. This allows you to see changes immediately without waiting for a revalidation period to pass.
188	
189	#### Revalidation frequency
190	
191	- The lowest `revalidate` across each layout and page of a single route will determine the revalidation frequency of the _entire_ route. This ensures that child pages are revalidated as frequently as their parent layouts.
192	- Individual `fetch` requests can set a lower `revalidate` than the route's default `revalidate` to increase the revalidation frequency of the entire route. This allows you to dynamically opt-in to more frequent revalidation for certain routes based on some criteria.
193	
194	## On-demand revalidation
195	
196	To revalidate cached data after an event, use [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) or [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath) in a [Server Action](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route).
197	
198	### Tagging cached data
199	
200	Tag `fetch` requests with `next.tags` to enable on-demand cache invalidation:
201	
202	```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" switcher
203	export async function getUserById(id: string) {
204	  const data = await fetch(`https://...`, {
205	    next: { tags: ['user'] },
206	  })
207	}
208	```
209	
210	```jsx filename="app/lib/data.js" switcher
211	export async function getUserById(id) {
212	  const data = await fetch(`https://...`, {
213	    next: { tags: ['user'] },
214	  })
215	}
216	```
217	
218	For non-`fetch` functions, `unstable_cache` also accepts a `tags` option (see [example above](#unstable_cache-for-non-fetch-functions)).
219	
220	### `revalidateTag`
221	
222	Invalidate cached data by tag using [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag):
223	
224	```tsx filename="app/lib/actions.ts" switcher
225	import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache'
226	
227	export async function updateUser(id: string) {
228	  // Mutate data
229	  revalidateTag('user', 'max')
230	}
231	```
232	
233	```jsx filename="app/lib/actions.js" switcher
234	import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache'
235	
236	export async function updateUser(id) {
237	  // Mutate data
238	  revalidateTag('user', 'max')
239	}
240	```
241	
242	### `revalidatePath`
243	
244	Invalidate all cached data for a specific route path using [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath):
245	
246	```tsx filename="app/lib/actions.ts" switcher
247	import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache'
248	
249	export async function updateUser(id: string) {
250	  // Mutate data
251	  revalidatePath('/profile')
252	}
253	```
254	
255	```jsx filename="app/lib/actions.js" switcher
256	import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache'
257	
258	export async function updateUser(id) {
259	  // Mutate data
260	  revalidatePath('/profile')
261	}
262	```
263	
264	## Deduplicating requests
265	
266	If you are not using `fetch` (which is [automatically memoized](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/fetch#memoization)), and instead using an ORM or database directly, you can wrap your data access with the [React `cache`](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) function to deduplicate requests within a single render pass:
267	
268	```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" switcher
269	import { cache } from 'react'
270	import { db, posts, eq } from '@/lib/db'
271	
272	export const getPost = cache(async (id: string) => {
273	  const post = await db.query.posts.findFirst({
274	    where: eq(posts.id, parseInt(id)),
275	  })
276	})
277	```
278	
279	```jsx filename="app/lib/data.js" switcher
280	import { cache } from 'react'
281	import { db, posts, eq } from '@/lib/db'
282	
283	export const getPost = cache(async (id) => {
284	  const post = await db.query.posts.findFirst({
285	    where: eq(posts.id, parseInt(id)),
286	  })
287	})
288	```
289	
290	## Preloading data
291	
292	You can preload data by creating a utility function that you eagerly call above blocking requests. This lets you initiate data fetching early, so the data is already available by the time the component renders.
293	
294	Combine the [`server-only` package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/server-only) with React's [`cache`](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) to create a reusable preload utility:
295	
296	```ts filename="utils/get-item.ts" switcher
297	import { cache } from 'react'
298	import 'server-only'
299	
300	export const getItem = cache(async (id: string) => {
301	  // ...
302	})
303	
304	export const preload = (id: string) => {
305	  void getItem(id)
306	}
307	```
308	
309	```js filename="utils/get-item.js" switcher
310	import { cache } from 'react'
311	import 'server-only'
312	
313	export const getItem = cache(async (id) => {
314	  // ...
315	})
316	
317	export const preload = (id) => {
318	  void getItem(id)
319	}
320	```
321	
322	Then call `preload()` before any blocking work so the data starts loading immediately:
323	
324	```tsx filename="app/item/[id]/page.tsx" switcher
325	import { getItem, preload, checkIsAvailable } from '@/lib/data'
326	
327	export default async function Page({
328	  params,
329	}: {
330	  params: Promise<{ id: string }>
331	}) {
332	  const { id } = await params
333	  // Start loading item data
334	  preload(id)
335	  // Perform another asynchronous task
336	  const isAvailable = await checkIsAvailable()
337	
338	  return isAvailable ? <Item id={id} /> : null
339	}
340	
341	async function Item({ id }: { id: string }) {
342	  const result = await getItem(id)
343	  // ...
344	}
345	```
346	
347	```jsx filename="app/item/[id]/page.js" switcher
348	import { getItem, preload, checkIsAvailable } from '@/lib/data'
349	
350	export default async function Page({ params }) {
351	  const { id } = await params
352	  // Start loading item data
353	  preload(id)
354	  // Perform another asynchronous task
355	  const isAvailable = await checkIsAvailable()
356	
357	  return isAvailable ? <Item id={id} /> : null
358	}
359	
360	async function Item({ id }) {
361	  const result = await getItem(id)
362	  // ...
363	}
364	```
365	
366	## Statically generating dynamic routes
367	
368	To prerender dynamic routes with [`generateStaticParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params) and revalidate them over time, see the [Incremental Static Regeneration](/docs/app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration) guide.
369
